method_note: FAST MODE, one round. Reused facts copied with sources from the 13 Nov packs (reused: true). New facts read today from official sources only.

facts.claim: France: 'Under French Law THE CERTIFICATE (which is produced in FRENCH by the Australian Embassy in Paris) is valid for only 90 days after the date of issue.' The certificate is the Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (certificat de coutume ou de non-opposition au mariage).
facts.authority: Australian Embassy Paris issues the CNI; the mairie confirms what it accepts.

facts.claim: France: a marriage must take place at a Town Hall (mairie) to be legally recognised, and at least one of the applicants must be a French citizen or a legal resident of France. The Embassy tells couples to contact the mairie directly for its requirements.
facts.authority: Australian Embassy France; the mairie confirms the current process.

facts.claim: France: the Australian Embassy says to check with local authorities whether the birth certificate has to be less than six months old. Processing of the CNI can take up to ten working days. A CNI already issued in English by a DFAT office in Australia must be translated by a sworn translator.
facts.authority: Australian Embassy France; the mairie confirms.
facts.use_note: Write 'many mairies ask for a birth certificate issued within the last six months; confirm with yours', not as a national rule.

facts.claim: France: witnesses are compulsory. The couple choose 2 witnesses minimum and 4 maximum; they are witnesses of the marriage, not of one partner.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.authority: Service Public (Code civil article 37); the mairie confirms.

facts.claim: France: witnesses must be at least 18 (or emancipated) on the day. They can be family members or not, of any sex, and of foreign nationality. A witness who does not understand French may be assisted by an interpreter of their choice.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative

facts.claim: France: witnesses are declared during the pre-marriage formalities (names, date and place of birth, occupation, address, copy of ID) and can be changed until the ceremony. Each witness must present the original of their identity document on the day and stay until they sign the register.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative

facts.claim: France, which commune: the marriage can be celebrated in the commune where one of the couple has their domicile or their residence, or in the commune where a parent (father or mother only) of one of them has their residence. Page wording: 'Le mariage peut être célébré dans la commune où l'un de vous 2 a sa résidence' and 'dans la commune de la résidence d'un des parents (père ou mère uniquement) de l'un de vous 2. Ce peut être, par exemple, une résidence secondaire.'
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.authority: Service Public; the mairie of the chosen commune confirms.
facts.use_note: A parent's holiday home counts as a residence. Still subject to F-002 and F-009 for two foreigners.

facts.claim: France, residence period: 'La résidence doit être établie par au moins 1 mois d'habitation continue à la date de la publication des bans.' The same 1-month continuous rule applies to a parent's residence. Proof must be in your name (or the parent's name) in that commune, for example an energy bill, home insurance certificate or rent receipt dated more than 1 month before the banns.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.use_note: Residency answer: at least 1 month of continuous living in the commune (yours or a parent's) by the date the banns are published.

facts.claim: France, two foreigners who do not live in France: 'Que vous soyez un couple de sexe différent ou de même sexe, si vous êtes tous les 2 étrangers et que vous n'habitez pas en France, ... le mariage en France d'un couple étranger est possible uniquement dans les lieux suivants : Consulat de votre pays d'origine; Commune d'une collectivité d'outre-mer (Com) ou de Nouvelle-Calédonie.'
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.authority: Service Public; consistent with Australian Embassy France (F-002).
facts.use_note: Key line for the article: two Australians not living in France cannot marry at a mainland French mairie. Note the consulate option refers to the couple's own country's consulate; Australia does not perform marriages at its consulates as far as we know, so do not suggest it without a source (see needs).

facts.claim: France, certificat de coutume: a foreign national 'devez présenter un certificat de coutume', generally issued by your embassy or consulate. It states the foreign rules applicable to marriage, a document proving civil status and a document proving you are not already married. A certificat de célibat is requested when your country cannot supply up-to-date documents.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.authority: Service Public; for Australians the Australian Embassy Paris issues it (F-001).

facts.claim: France, marriage file (dossier de mariage): before any appointment, contact the marriage commune with your names, sex, date and commune of birth and your parents' names. The file includes ID, proof of domicile or residence dated more than 1 month at the date of the banns, witness details, each partner's occupation (in French), each parent's identity, address and occupation, any common children, and contact details. Foreign nationals may be asked for documents specific to their nationality, including the certificat de coutume.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.authority: Service Public; the mairie sets the final list.
facts.use_note: Summary of the page's lists, not every item. Birth certificate recency: see F-003.

facts.claim: France, hearing: 'L'officier d'état civil vous auditionne tous les 2 ensemble' and may also ask for individual interviews. 'Cette audition est obligatoire', with exceptions (the page lists cases, including where it is not needed). If one partner lives abroad, the hearing may be carried out by the competent diplomatic or consular authority. If needed the registrar can refer to the procureur, who has 15 days to let the marriage proceed or oppose it, or may set a delay of up to 1 month, renewable, for an enquiry.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.use_note: Medium because the exceptions list was not read in full this round. Write 'the registrar will usually interview you together'.

facts.claim: France, banns: the marriage is announced by publication des bans, notices posted at the door of the mairie of the marriage and the mairie of the domicile of either partner, 'pendant 10 jours'. The notice gives the names, occupations, domicile or residence of each partner and the place of the marriage. A dispensation from publication can be requested from the procureur. 'Le mariage doit être célébré dans l'année qui suit l'expiration du délai de 10 jours.'
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.use_note: 10 days of banns, then the wedding must happen within one year.

facts.claim: France, religious ceremony: 'Il est interdit de célébrer un mariage religieux avant le mariage civil.' (It is forbidden to celebrate a religious marriage before the civil marriage.)
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.use_note: A church or other religious wedding in France must come after the civil ceremony at the mairie. A symbolic (non-religious, non-legal) celebration is a different thing; do not conflate.

facts.claim: France, where and who: 'Le mariage doit être célébré à la mairie, dans une salle ouverte au public.' The mayor may hold it in any communal building in the commune (for example a salle des fêtes), though the procureur can object. 'La célébration doit être faite par le maire ou un adjoint', in the presence of both partners and their witnesses. A translator-interpreter may be present (at your cost if paid).
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.use_note: So the legal ceremony cannot be at a chateau or vineyard; that would be the symbolic celebration.

facts.claim: France, documents after the wedding: 'Un livret de famille vous est délivré.' In the following days you can ask the mairie for an extract or full copy (copie intégrale) of the acte de mariage.
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.authority: Service Public; the mairie issues both.

facts.claim: France, same-sex couples: the official marriage page addresses couples 'de sexe différent ou de même sexe' throughout, and gives special commune options for a couple where one is French and they live in a country that does not allow same-sex marriage (French commune of birth or last residence, or a parent's commune).
facts.publisher: Service Public, Direction de l'information legale et administrative
facts.use_note: Supports 'same-sex couples can marry in France on the same terms'. The 2013 date was NOT sourced this round (see needs).

needs.detail: Not read from an official source this round. Source it from legifrance.gouv.fr (loi du 17 mai 2013) or service-public before printing the year.
F930 lists cases where the audition is not required; the list was not read in full (F-012).

F-009 says two foreigners not living in France may marry at their own country's consulate. Whether Australian missions in France perform marriages was not checked. Do not suggest it without an official source.
